head.h1: Grazing Table Catering in Dubai — Menus, Prices and What's Included

opening_paragraph: Grazing table catering in Dubai from myCHEF starts at AED 150 per person built and styled on site, or AED 700 with a chef serving through the event. It is a styled, abundant centrepiece guests graze all evening. The display layers cheeses, charcuterie, dips, fruit and breads. A vetted private chef designs the menu, builds the display, serves and clears, so you host without ever hovering over a platter. Tell us your date, guest count and venue, and during our published business hours your itemised proposal comes back promptly.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What does a grazing table include?
new_paragraphs: A grazing table is one long, generously loaded display that guests pick at throughout your event, instead of a plated course or a seated meal. The classic spread layers a range of soft and hard cheeses, cured and halal charcuterie, warm and cold dips, seasonal fruit, olives and antipasti, and a run of breads, crackers and crudités down the centre. MyCHEF builds the whole thing on site — the abundance, the height and colour, the edible flowers and greenery — so the table itself becomes the room's focal point. Every grazing table food catering dubai order is made to your headcount, so nothing runs short and nothing is a token garnish. Because it is grazed, not served in sittings, it keeps a party moving and lets people eat when they like, which is exactly why it suits receptions, launches and long celebrations.
How much does it cost for a grazing table?

A delivered grazing board starts at AED 90 per person from 10 guests, a table built and styled on site at AED 150 per person from 20 guests, and a table worked by a chef through the event at AED 700 per person. Multiply by your guest count for the table total; the minimum order is AED 900 and 5% VAT is added.
What is the difference between a grazing board and a grazing table?

Scale and service. A board is one large platter for a small gathering or a boardroom; a table is a full styled surface, built in sections, refreshed during the event and intended as the centrepiece of the room.
Can you do an afternoon tea grazing table?

Yes — finger sandwiches, scones with clotted cream and preserves, small pastries and a tea service, laid out the same generous way instead of tiered on stands. It is a common request for bridal showers and ladies' gatherings.
What is included in a grazing table?

Included is menu design, a vetted chef, on-site styling and setup of the display, service through your event, and cleanup where relevant — cheeses, charcuterie, dips, fruit, breads and crackers arranged as one abundant centrepiece.
How many guests does a grazing table serve?

A delivered board suits 10 guests upward and a table built on site starts at 20, while a chef-served table has no headcount minimum, so an intimate gathering works too. At the other end we build for a hundred or more, sizing the length of the table, the volume of food and the number of chefs to your headcount.
Can the grazing table be halal, vegan or allergy-friendly?

Yes. Halal charcuterie and cheeses are standard on request, and we build vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free and nut-free versions from the same styled format. Tell us the dietary needs and we design around them.
Is grazing table catering full-service or drop-off?
It is a full-service arrangement by default — the chef arrives to build, style, serve and clear. A simpler delivered option can be discussed for smaller budgets and casual gatherings.
How far in advance should I book?

About 72 hours for a delivered board or a standard styled table, 3 to 5 days where a chef works the table, and 5 to 7 days for a bespoke menu or a larger event. Weddings and corporate productions want 7 to 14 days or more. Once you send your date, guest count and venue, an itemised proposal usually comes back within one business day.
How is a grazing table different from a private chef dinner?
A grazing table is a grazed, shared centrepiece instead of a seated, multi-course meal. If you are weighing the two, see private chef vs catering for how the formats and costs compare.

For grazing table catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements , and you can pair a grazing table with our finger food or dessert table , or explore all event catering .

MyCHEF arranges grazing tables anywhere in Dubai, matched to your occasion, guest count and venue. We regularly build them in villas across Palm Jumeirah, Emirates Hills, Jumeirah and Arabian Ranches, in apartments in Dubai Marina, JBR, Downtown and Business Bay, on yacht charters, and in offices across DIFC and Business Bay. The chef and team travel to you with everything needed, so the setting can be a private garden, a rooftop, a boardroom or a beach house. Wherever you are in the emirate, the styling, the menu and the service are adapted to the space and the crowd.

Outside Dubai — Sharjah, Ajman, Abu Dhabi — coverage depends on the partner and the date rather than on a fixed service area, because the table is built on site and the team has to travel with it. Send the address with your enquiry and we tell you before you commit whether it can be served from the Dubai network and what the travel adds to the quote. A straight answer either way beats a booking that turns into a problem on the morning.

add_block.new_heading: Grazing table meaning, and how a grazing board differs
new_paragraphs: The meaning is literal: guests graze. Instead of courses arriving in sittings, the food is laid out as one continuous display and people help themselves for as long as the event runs. Nothing is portioned per plate, so the table has to be built to keep looking generous after the first hour, which is why abundance and height are part of the brief rather than decoration.

A grazing board is the same idea at a smaller scale. It is a single large board or platter — one cheese group, a few cured meats, a dip, fruit, crackers — sized for a coffee morning, a small home gathering or a boardroom of eight to twelve. A grazing table is a full surface, several metres of it at a wedding, built in sections with warm elements and refreshed during service. If you are feeding a room of fifteen at home, ask for a board; if the food is meant to be the centrepiece people photograph, ask for the table.

add_block.new_heading: Grazing table ideas that work in Dubai
new_paragraphs: Most hosts arrive with a picture rather than a menu, so here are the directions that come up most often. A Mediterranean table leans on whipped feta, muhammara, marinated vegetables, olives, grissini and warm flatbread. An Arabic-leaning build runs labneh, halloumi, dates, dried fruit, nuts and manakish alongside the cheeses. A dessert grazing table takes the same format into pastries, chocolate, fruit and small cakes for a birthday or a baby shower.

An afternoon tea grazing table is the other request we see, usually for bridal showers and ladies' gatherings: finger sandwiches, scones with clotted cream and preserves, small pastries and a tea service, laid the same generous way rather than tiered on stands. For a summer event, ideas that survive the climate matter more than ideas that photograph well, so we weight the table toward cheeses, cured items, breads and dips that hold, and bring the delicate elements out in waves.

Corporate grazing table catering dubai fits product launches, office milestones and networking evenings, where a shared table gets people talking instead of queuing at a buffet. For at-home celebrations, grazing table party catering dubai and grazing table home catering dubai turn a villa or apartment into the venue, with the chef arriving, styling and clearing so your kitchen stays yours. Birthdays, baby showers, brunches and festive gatherings all take the same treatment — we scale the length of the table and the number of hands to the guest count and the room.

add_block.new_heading: What is on a grazing table menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A grazing table menu dubai is built around abundance and contrast, then tailored to your guests and any dietary needs. A typical build runs through a cheese section (brie, aged cheddar, halloumi, labneh), a charcuterie section with halal options, warm and cold dips such as hummus, muhammara and whipped feta, fresh and dried fruit, nuts, olives, marinated vegetables, and a bakery run of sourdough, crackers, grissini and crudités. From there we adapt: fully vegetarian and vegan tables, gluten-free and dairy-free versions, nut-free spreads, and Arabic or Mediterranean-leaning displays. Halal charcuterie and cheeses are standard on request. Because a private grazing table chef dubai assembles it fresh on site, seasonal produce and warm elements — spiced nuts, baked cheese, fresh flatbread — go out at their best instead of sitting under cling film. Tell us your guest profile and we shape the menu around it.

add_block.new_heading: The full grazing table menu, section by section
new_paragraphs: This is the working bank the chefs build a table from, laid out in the order the table itself is composed — the boards and the cheese first, then the mezze and the cold bites, then the warm things that come out in waves, and the sweet end last. Nothing here is a fixed package. You mark what your room will eat, the chef says what is good that week and what will hold in the heat, and the agreed list goes into the written quote before anything is confirmed. A board for ten takes a handful of lines from two or three sections; a wedding table takes something from most of them.

One structural note shapes the whole build: the charcuterie line is halal, and it is specified that way from the start, not swapped out at the end. Turkey ham, pastrami, cured beef bresaola and smoked poultry carry the cured section, and pork does not appear.
The signature board and the components it is built from

These are the whole builds — what a board or a table is composed of before anything else is added. Boards, risers, bowls, linen, greenery and glassware are part of the deliverable, not a separate line.
Signature grazing platter: artisan cheeses, halal charcuterie, gourmet crackers, antipasti, fresh and dried fruits, spiced nuts and seasonal garnishes.
House-cured meats, imported cheeses, homemade pickles, fruits and crackers: the fuller build, for when the table is the meal.
International Grazing Table: the mixed build, drawing cheeses and bites from several regions, not one.
Slate Grazing Platter: the same components presented on slate, for a darker, more formal room.
Mexican Grazing Board: a regional build for a themed party.
Garden Vegetable Crudités: raw and blanched vegetables cut for dipping, run down the centre.
Crudité Tzatziki Dip: the yoghurt, cucumber and herb dip that goes with them.
Beetroot hummus with organic veggie sticks: the plant-forward corner of the board.
Antipasti Skewers: marinated vegetables, olives and cheese threaded onto sticks so guests lift a portion cleanly.
Aged Cheddar, Almond & Stuffed Olive: a hard-cheese bite for the cheese section.
Sun-Dried Tomato, Burrata & Rocket: the soft-cheese counterpoint.
Burrata Tomato Eggplant: burrata with tomato and eggplant, one of the anchor bowls.
Cheese-led cold bites tucked along the boards
These sit between the whole cheeses and the crackers, and they are what stops a cheese section reading like a supermarket platter. Most are one bite, so they hold their shape while people talk.
3 Jelly Caprese & Burrata: burrata with three fruit and tomato jellies.
Comté Sablé & Cherry: a savoury shortbread base under Comté and cherry.
Date & Goat Cheese: the Gulf pairing that disappears fastest off a Dubai table.
Black Fig, Goat Cheese & Rocca: black fig with goat cheese and rocket.
Endives with Blue Cheese & Walnut: endive leaves as the base, blue cheese and walnut on top.
Labneh Millefeuille: layered labneh, built by hand and not spooned.
Feta & Sun Dried Tomato Madeleine: a savoury madeleine carrying feta and sun-dried tomato.
Watermelon Feta, Grenadine Molasses: watermelon and feta finished with grenadine molasses.
Chèvre Cheesecake: a small savoury goat-cheese cheesecake.
Persian feta, thyme waffle, truffled honey, fig: sweet and salty in the same bite.
Shiitake, Black Truffle & Charred Brie Macaron: a savoury macaron shell around brie and truffle.
Gorgonzola Tartlet: gorgonzola with quince paste and celery in a short pastry case.
Honey-Glazed Fig on Aish Bulbul: honey-glazed fig with goat curd and pomegranate seeds.
Compressed Watermelon: compressed watermelon with goat curd and olive soil.
Artichoke Bruschetta: artichoke with olive and parmesan on toasted bread.
Beetroot Napoleon: layered beetroot, built tall so it reads on a crowded board.
Arabic Mezze Crisp: the mezze flavours on a crisp base, for guests circulating away from the table.
English Cucumber Sandwich: the plainest thing on the table, and the first to go.
Beiruti Hummus Crostini: Beiruti hummus on crostini.
Green Gazpacho Shooter: chilled green gazpacho, poured into glasses.
The Arabic and Levantine end of the table

In Dubai this section carries a table more reliably than any imported cheese does. Dips go into shallow bowls with warm bread stacked beside them, and the hot kebabs come out through the event instead of sitting from the start.
Hummus Traditional: chickpea and tahini, the anchor bowl.
Mutabel: smoked aubergine with tahini and yoghurt.
Babaganoush: the chunkier, sharper aubergine dip.
Tabouleh: parsley, mint, tomato and bulgur, cut fine.
Cheese Sambousek: fried pastry parcels filled with cheese.
Spinach & Cheese Fatayer: baked spinach and cheese pastries.
Cheese Burek: layered pastry with cheese.
Falafel Rocks: falafel with tahini alongside.
Beetroot Kibbeh: the vegan kibbeh, with tomato sugo.
Lamb Kibbeh: lamb kibbeh with sumac mint yoghurt.
Arabic Shish Tawook: marinated chicken skewers off the grill.
Kofta — Beef & Lamb: minced kofta skewers.
Harra Barra Kebab: the spiced kebab, for a table that wants some heat.
Chapli Kebab (Beef / Lamb): the flat, spiced patty kebab.
Sheekh Kebab — Beef / Chicken: minced seekh, grilled to order.
Cold seafood, set on ice at one end
Seafood is the section the climate argues with, so it sits over ice at the end furthest from any door, and it is replenished in small batches instead of laid out in full at the start.
Smoked Salmon with Citrus Cream: with pickled radish on sourdough bread.
Smoked Salmon with Cream Cheese & Chives: the version most guests recognise, done properly.
Salmon Carpaccia with Shaved Parmesan: thin salmon under shaved parmesan.
Salmon Blinis: salmon on a warm blini.
Black Blini & Smoked Salmon: a squid-ink blini under smoked salmon.
Tarama Blinis: taramasalata on blini.
Seabass & Fennel Ceviche: cured seabass with fennel.
Prawn Salad Verrine: with coriander mango and wasabi mayonnaise, served in a glass.
Tuna Tataki Skewers: seared tuna, sliced onto skewers.
Crab Cucumber Gaspacho: chilled cucumber gazpacho with crab.
Salmon & Prawn Nori Roll: salmon and prawn rolled in nori.
Quail Egg & Salmontini Royale: quail egg with salmon, one clean bite.
Cold meat and poultry bites
Roast Beef with Horseradish Sauce: rare roast beef with horseradish.
Smoked Chicken & Apricot: smoked chicken cut with apricot.
Buttered Asparagus & Turkey Ham Blankets: asparagus wrapped in turkey ham.
Beef Tataki: seared and sliced thin.
Seared Angus Tenderloin: Angus tenderloin, seared and served cold.
Peppered Pastarmi on Potato Rösti: with curry mayonnaise.
Lemongrass Chicken Roulade: with tomato pesto and coriander.
Chicken Breast on Brioche Croute: with chermoula sauce and cilantro.
Cajun Chicken Tartlet: with guacamole and chipotle sauce.
Peking Duck Pancake: with hoisin sauce, rolled in front of guests where a chef is working the table.
Warm bites brought out in waves — vegetarian and vegan

Warm elements are the reason the chef-served tier exists. They are cooked or finished on site and carried out through the event, so the table gains something new every half hour instead of slowly going cold.
Parmesan Arancini: fried risotto balls with parmesan.
Mushroom & Truffle Arancini: the truffled version of the same.
Wild Mushroom & Truffle Tart: wild mushroom and truffle in short pastry.
Mushroom Vol Au Vent: creamed mushroom in a puff pastry case.
Aubergine & Tahini Tart: roast aubergine with tahini.
Sundried Tomato & Feta Cheese Tart: sun-dried tomato and feta, baked.
Goat Cheese Quiche: with olive and sundried tomato.
Spanakopita: spinach and feta in filo.
Cheese Stuffed Gougère: choux buns filled with cheese.
Truffle Stuffed Gougère: the truffled gougère.
Parmesan Cheese Beignet: fried parmesan beignets, eaten straight out of the pan.
Spring Rolls: with soy dip.
Mini Falafel Bites: with tahini dip.
Vegetable Pakora: with coconut chutney.
Cocktail Vegetable Spring Roll: the smaller, one-bite roll.
Dukkah scented quinoa burger: with onion beetroot relish and coriander mayonnaise, vegan.
Warm meat and seafood bites
Wagyu beef kofta: wagyu mince, grilled.
Middle Eastern Spiced Lamb Tenderloin: lamb tenderloin with Middle Eastern spicing.
Panko-Crusted Lamb Cigar: lamb rolled and crumbed, fried to order.
Chipotle Chicken Skewers: with chimichurri dip.
Indonesian Chicken Satay Skewer: satay with its own sauce.
Chicken Yakitori: glazed and grilled chicken skewers.
Oriental Lamb Meatballs: with tomato onion sauce.
Truffled Chicken & Mushroom Ravioli: a heavier bite, for a table that replaces dinner.
Harissa Spiced Prawn: prawns with harissa.
Prawns Sweet Chili Skewers: prawn skewers with sweet chilli.
Shrimp Tempura: fried to order, so it goes out immediately.
Sesame-Crusted Asian Crab Cake: crab cake in a sesame crust.
Maryland Crab Cakes: the classic crab cake.
Salmon fish cake: small enough to eat standing up.
Vegan components, built as their own run of the table
Vegan guests do not get a bowl of crudités in the corner. The vegan items take their own stretch of the table with their own boards and serving tools, which is better hosting and a cleaner build.
Rice Paper Roll: with Chinese mushrooms and vegan XO sauce.
Rice Paper Roll with Som Tam Salad: with sweet chilli sauce.
Pumpkin Hummus Cone: with pomegranate seeds.
Eggplant Tartlet: with tomato and Gran Vegiano.
Cherry Tomato with Avocado: a plain, good bite that suits most tables.
Beetroot tartare: raw beetroot, dressed and shaped.
Truffle Edamame: edamame with truffle.
Vegan Carrot Cake: the vegan option at the sweet end.
Sliders, buns and one-bite sandwiches along the table
Mini Caprese Wagyu Slider: wagyu with mozzarella and tomato.
Mini Roast Beef Burger: roast beef in a small bun.
Angus Beef & Melt Cheese: Angus with melted cheese.
Mini Croque Monsieur: the toasted ham and cheese, cut down to a bite.
Truffle Brie Cheese Bun: brie and truffle in a soft bun.
Brie Apricot Jam Bun: brie with apricot jam.
Smoked Salmon Capers Bun: smoked salmon and capers.
Egg Avocado Bun: egg and avocado.
Chicken Caesar Bun: the Caesar, in bun form.
Labneh Zaatar Croissant: labneh and zaatar in a small croissant.
Bresaola Croissant: cured beef bresaola in a croissant.
Cucumber, Feta & Dill: the light one, for a hot afternoon.
Nibbles pre-set before the table opens
These go into bowls along the run and on the side tables before guests arrive, so the room has something to reach for while the first drinks are poured.
Middle Eastern perfumed dates: scented dates, in bowls down the table.
Assorted candied Asian nuts: the sweet-salted nut mix.
Orange, fennel, scented olives: olives dressed with orange and fennel.
Spicy edamame: edamame with chilli.
Wasabi and miso salted popcorn, bonito flakes: the one guests comment on.
Pimentos, garlic chips, sherry vinegar: pimentos with garlic chips and sherry vinegar.
Verrines, shots and spoons
Traditional Gazpacho: chilled tomato gazpacho in a glass.
Green Gazpacho: the green, herb-led version.
Quinoa tabbouleh in mini shots: tabbouleh built on quinoa, in shot glasses.
Gazpacho Shrimps: gazpacho with shrimp.
Shrimp Cocktail: served in glassware along the table.
Panna Cotta Shooter: panna cotta in a shot glass, at the sweet end.
The sweet end of the table

A dessert grazing table is the same format taken into pastry, and it is a common brief on its own for birthdays and baby showers. On a savoury table this section is built at one end and opened later in the evening.
Fruit skewers: seasonal fruit on skewers, the easiest thing to keep looking generous.
Dark chocolate-dipped figs: figs dipped in dark chocolate.
Date-energy balls rolled in coconut: dates rolled and finished in coconut.
Kunafa: the Levantine pastry, cut into small squares.
Basboosa: semolina cake in small pieces.
Signature Toffee Date Pudding: with caramel sauce.
Croissant Umm Ali: umm ali built on croissant.
Lemon Meringue Tartlets: lemon curd under torched meringue.
Chocolate Macaron: macarons, coloured to the styling.
Sicilian Cannoli: filled to order so the shell stays crisp.
Jivara Chocolate Raspberry Tartlet: Jivara chocolate with raspberry.
Orange Blossom Profiterole: choux with orange blossom.
Candied Kumquat Cheesecake: small cheesecakes with candied kumquat.
Lavender & Coconut Panna Cotta Pot: panna cotta in individual pots.
Peach Raspberry Tart: peach and raspberry, vegan.
Citrus Pecan Delight: citrus and pecan, vegan.
Gulab Jamun: warm, in syrup.
Jalebi: fried and syruped, made close to the table.
Live stations you can set beside the table

A station is a chef and a piece of equipment working in front of guests, quoted separately from the table because it needs its own setup, power and hands. One is usually enough — the interaction is the point, not the extra food.
Live Carvery Station: honey miso glazed roasts, sautéed greens, butternut pumpkin and truffle celeriac purées, carved to order.
Shawarma Station: protein on the vertical rotisserie, wrapped in saj bread with accompaniments.
Sushi Station: live maki and nigiri preparation at the counter.
Pizza Station: Harissa Lamb, BBQ Chicken, Diavola, Margherita, Quattro Formaggi.
Taqueria Station: tortillas straight from the grill with carne asada, chicken confit, beef cheek and tuna ceviche, guests mixing their own sauces.
Sliders Station: beef, chicken, mushroom and vegetarian, griddled to order.
Barbecue / Robata station: skewers over charcoal, set outdoors.
Interactive Hot Pot: guests cook their own proteins, vegetables, noodles, rice and broths.
Mocktails, juices and hot drinks alongside
Jallab: the date and rose-water classic, poured over ice with pine nuts.
Kamardine: apricot, the Ramadan staple.
Rose Sharbat: rose syrup, long and cold.
Jal Jeera: cumin-spiced and savoury.
Lassi: yoghurt-based, sweet or salted.
Lemon Mint: the one that empties first in summer.
Cucumber Cooler: cucumber-led and light.
Tropical Kale Juice: the green juice.
Antioxidant Blast Juice: the fruit-forward blend.
Arabic Coffee: served with the dates.
Moroccan Tea: mint tea, poured tall.
Indian Masala Tea: spiced chai.
Dietary requirements on a shared table

A grazing table is an open, shared display, which makes dietary planning a design question, not a footnote. Halal charcuterie and cheeses are standard on request, vegetarian and vegan items are built as their own runs with their own boards and serving tools, and a fully vegetarian or fully vegan table is a normal brief. Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event — on a shared surface, tell us early enough that the affected items can be plated separately instead of set into the display.

Book a delivered board or a standard styled table about 72 hours ahead; allow 3 to 5 days where a chef works the table, and 5 to 7 days for a bespoke menu or a larger event.
Allow 7 to 14 days or more for a wedding or a corporate production.
Confirm what goes on the grazing table catering menu 7 days out, once the count settles.
Ask for special diets up front; grazing table catering plates are planned, not improvised inside 48 hours .
Check loading and access details; allow 2 hours of grazing table catering setup on site.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of grazing table catering service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. If your grazing table date is close, tell us anyway - the team checks partner availability case by case.

add_block.new_heading: Which grazing format suits your event?
new_paragraphs: Format What you get Service staff Minimum From
Grazing board, delivered One large board or platter, delivered ready to put out None 10 guests AED 90 per person
Grazing table, built and styled on site The full display assembled, styled and left looking generous 1–2 20 guests AED 150 per person
Grazing table with a chef through the event Warm elements cooked on site, the table refreshed, served and cleared 2 and above No headcount minimum AED 700 per person

Minimum order value is AED 900, and 5% VAT is added to the total. The jump between the rows is service, not quantity: at AED 90 the food arrives ready, at AED 150 someone builds and styles it in your room, and at AED 700 a chef stays with it, cooks the warm elements and keeps the table looking the way it did when the first guest walked in.

add_block.new_heading: How much does it cost for a grazing table?
new_paragraphs: Grazing tables are quoted per head and then multiplied by your guest count, so the cost of the table itself depends entirely on how many people it has to feed. A table built and styled on site starts at AED 150 per person with a minimum of 20 guests; a delivered grazing board starts at AED 90 per person from 10 guests; and a grazing table kept, refreshed and served by a chef through the event starts at AED 700 per person. The smallest booking we take is the AED 900 minimum order, and 5% VAT is added to every total.

There is no useful average cost of a grazing table, and any figure quoted as one should be treated carefully. The same length of table can double in price on cheese alone — imported and aged cheeses against local, cured charcuterie against a simpler cold selection — and styling, rental boards, linen and flowers sit on top of the food. For a wedding, where the table is usually longer, refreshed twice and photographed, expect to sit at the upper end of whichever tier you choose. Take your guest count, multiply by the per-head figure for the format you want, add VAT, and you have the real number before anyone quotes you.

add_block.new_heading: Why book your grazing table with myCHEF
new_paragraphs: MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the evening, we carry the work. MyCHEF is implementing a structured partner verification framework covering identity and licence checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing performance review — a continuous standard, not a one-time tick. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so we match each event to the chef whose background fits it.

For a grazing table, that is often Marco Rossi , our Italian and Mediterranean specialist, whose feel for cheeses, cured meats, antipasti and generous, colourful presentation is exactly what this format lives on — he designs each table as a collaboration with the host and styles it to the room. We have run grazing table catering alongside villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas across Dubai. Client reviews are added as events run.
